title: Cai Lun presents improved papermaking to the Han court
summary: In the first year of the Yuanxing era (105 CE) the Eastern Han court official Cai Lun presented a paper made from tree bark, hemp waste, rags and fishing nets to Emperor He, who praised it. Paper existed earlier, so Cai Lun is better seen as improving materials and process than inventing paper.

uncertainty.note: The Hou Hanshu records the presentation in Yuanxing 1; earlier paper-like sheets are known, so this is an improvement and court presentation, not an origin of paper.

as_recorded.calendar: Chinese era name, Hou Hanshu biography of Cai Lun
as_recorded.value: 元兴元年奏上之 (Yuanxing 1: presented it to the throne)

where.modern_name: Luoyang, Henan, China (Eastern Han capital; the city, not the exact palace)
where.historical_name: Luoyang, capital of the Eastern Han dynasty

importance.justification: Marks the court adoption of an inexpensive writing material that later spread across Eurasia and transformed record keeping and book production.
